# Snippy

> A Manifest V3 Chrome extension for capturing UI/UX
> feedback on any website - comments, screenshots and captured page elements,
> with annotations, organized into a session, exported as a self-contained
> HTML report.

No backend and no site-side integration required - a reviewer clicks the
toolbar icon and Snippy opens in Chrome's side panel, where it stays across
pages, sites and tabs. The panel is React + TypeScript on the Recursica
design system, built by Vite.

## Reference documentation

- [README](README.md): What this is, how to build it, how to load it in
  Chrome, and the local development scripts.
- [ARCHITECTURE](ARCHITECTURE.md): The side panel and page helper
  lifecycle, the styling model, the storage data model, the report format,
  the build, release and CI, and the migration discipline required for any
  data-shape change.
- [AGENTS](AGENTS.md): Rules for AI agents making changes to this codebase -
  read this and ARCHITECTURE.md before planning a change.

## Layout

- `src/manifest.json` - The MV3 manifest, with the side panel
  (`side_panel.default_path`).
- `src/background.js` - Service worker: makes the toolbar icon open the
  side panel.
- `src/panel/` - The side panel (React + TypeScript): entry, components,
  session state, the active tab, the bridge to the page helper, and
  screenshot capture and cropping. Also the annotation editor's own tab
  (`annotate.html`), opened beside the reviewed page.
- `src/page/` - The page helper, injected into the reviewed page: capture
  overlays, element picking, the page's context, Recursica detection, and
  shortcuts pressed on the page. Built into `page.js`.
- `src/lib/` - Framework-free modules shared by both (`annotations`,
  `capture`, `captureFrame`, `element`, `environment`, `format`, `ids`,
  `links`, `overlay`, `pageApi`, `pageKey`, `pen`, `recursica`, `report`,
  `shortcuts`, `storage`, `types`).
- `recursica_variables_scoped.css`, `recursica_manifest.json`,
  `recursica_brand.json`, `recursica_tokens.json`, `recursica_ui-kit.json` -
  Snippy's Recursica Forge export (the theme), kept exactly as exported.
- `postcss.config.cjs` - Checks every Recursica CSS variable against the
  Forge export at build time.
- `src/report.css` - Styles the downloaded report only. Inlined into the
  panel's script at build time, not loaded at runtime.
- `src/ai-report-instructions.txt` - Hidden, AI-readable instructions
  explaining the report's structure, also inlined at build time.
- `vite.config.mts` - Two builds: the extension pages (`sidepanel.html`
  and `annotate.html`, with ES modules) and the page helper (one classic-script `page.js`).
- `scripts/make-icons.mjs` - Generates the four icon sizes in
  `src/icons/` from one source PNG (`npm run icons -- <source.png>`).
  `src/icons/source.svg` is the vector source of the icon.
- `scripts/package-extension.mjs` - Zips `dist/chrome` into
  `release-zips/snippy-chrome-v<version>.zip` (`npm run package-extension`).
- `scripts/lint-staged.config.cjs`, `.husky/` - The pre-commit hook that
  runs Prettier, ESLint and the type check on staged files.
- `eslint.config.mjs`, `.prettierignore` - Lint and format configuration.
- `build.js` - Runs both Vite builds, then assembles `dist/chrome` with
  `background.js`, the icons and the manifest.
- `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.node.json` - Type checking for `src/panel`,
  `src/page` and `src/lib`, and for the Vite config.
- `dist/` - Build output (git-ignored). Load `dist/chrome` as an unpacked
  extension to run it.
- `.changeset/` - Changesets config; this package is private and never
  published to npm, so versioning/changelog tracking is the point, not a
  registry publish.
- `.github/workflows/` - `pull-request.yml` (lint + build on every PR) and
  `release.yml` (Changesets' Version-Packages-PR flow).
